title: Bias a transistor-like stage at mid-supply
story: A voltage-controlled current source (gm = 40 mS) models a transistor. With 50 mV at its input it pulls current from the output node, and that current must come through the resistor from the 10 V supply. Choose that resistor so the output rests between 4.5 and 5.5 V, the middle of the supply.
hints: G1 pulls gm x v(in) = 0.04 S x 0.05 V = 2 mA out of the output node.
v(out) = 10 V - 2 mA x RC. For about 5 V you need a drop of about 5 V.
